title: Move the decimal with the unit
hook: 125 cents: how many euros is that?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Convert cents to euros using the stated unit relationship.

misconception: Converting cents to euros requires moving the decimal only one place.
objective: Convert cents to euros using the stated unit relationship.

claims.text: A euro contains 100 cents. A divides cents by 100; B deliberately divides by ten instead. Scaled model; unit arithmetic; 100 cents/€; B deliberately wrong.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Cents=125c, A=€1.25 and B=€12.5. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",100]; B=["/","x",10]; x denotes Cents. At x=125, A=1.25, B=12.5. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The denominator comes from the unit definition: one hundred cents per euro. Dividing by ten changes the amount by the wrong factor. Carry the unit alongside the digits so the decimal movement has a reason.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",100]; B=["/","x",10]; x denotes Cents. At x=125, A=1.25, B=12.5. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: A euro is 100 cents. How many euros is 305 cents? Correct: €3.05. Divide by 100, the number of cents per euro: €3.05. Dividing by ten gives €30.50.
